text:
Done. Every accepted release now records what its own descriptor says (kernel CatalogRecord: kind, title, description and the file it came from, creators, keywords, data types, licence, identifiers). ReleaseDescriptions (bids module) reads it: BIDS from dataset_description.json, the root README and the coverage summary; archive from archive_description.json. It is total: an unreadable descriptor yields missing fields.

How it is kept: NativeRepository.accept, the only caller of Catalog.accept, computes the record from the candidate and passes it in; PostgreSQL stores it in table release_catalog (migration V017) inside the acceptance transaction; a replay stores nothing. The reference catalog keeps the same map. Reads never write. A release accepted earlier has no row: NativeRepository.catalogRecord then derives the record from retained bytes with the same function, and the operator command repository rebuild-catalog STORAGE stores such records without replacing any. GET /v1/datasets/{d}/releases/{r}/catalog returns the record.

Criteria: 1 derived at acceptance from the accepted descriptor, missing fields explicit, project label untouched; 2 one row per release, R1 unchanged after R2, replay adds none; 3 the rebuilt record equals the stored one and release, manifest, interpretation and assessment identifiers are unchanged; 4 disclosure follows ADR 002: discovery still shows only the steward's label, and every record field needs ReadMetadata on that exact release; 5 the same two laws pass on the reference and PostgreSQL catalogs, for a BIDS study and an archive.

What the full gate caught: the first run passed every targeted suite and then failed 21 PolicyIntegrationSuite tests, because the witness and recovery code pin the exact schema version. Moved every pin to 17: PolicyBridge producer-schema, OrganizationRecoveryCli, the supported-schema sets in OrganizationRecovery and RecoveryBundleRestore, TransactionSuite, scripts/check-organization-recovery.py and docs/organization-recovery.md.

Evidence: CatalogCoverageSuite laws on both catalogs; CatalogRecordSuite (2) on PostgreSQL; scripts/check-postgres.sh passed (690 unit, 392 integration, crash and restore); packaged smoke test with a rebuild-catalog step; check-upgrade-compatibility.py against corpus-v2; check-organization-recovery.py passed 23 checks including a schema-17 backup cycle; check-console-backend.sh passed 13 scenarios.

Note for whoever runs the recovery rehearsal: it must be given the retained qualified harness, local-artifacts/recovery-20261102/artifacts/7549a6eb...jar. A harness built from today's test classes cannot drive the schema-13 predecessor package, because AccessContext gained a defaulted parameter on 17 November.

Follow-ups for other items: SEE3 searches these records; SEE4 reads them for the study page; data types here are coverage groups, so stimuli and phenotype appear as data types until SEE5 and SEE4 decide how to present them.
